scope: Read-only source, frozen metadata and produced small result-table/editorial audit. Did not execute patient scripts, process BAM/FASTQ records or edit root code. Seven synthetic in-memory records checked the repaired exact tracing predicate. Final release gate is supported by the separate independent count/transition audit.
passed_methods: count_compare iterates every unique frozen cohort key rather than reselecting jointly callable survivors. Original DNA counts/categories and original RNA columns are retained.

Coverage zero and nonzero depth below20 are explicit fields/counters; coverage-loss rows are written. Dominant pass numerators require new depth>=20, while original dominant denominator remains2873. No coverage loss is silently substituted as successful retention.
Dominant transition states are original retain90/below90 crossed with new below20/retain90/below90. These are assay-count state changes, not proof of a corrected allele or biological change.
New strong-allele screening preserves the declared both-depth>=50, DNA base<=2%, RNA base>=10% and >=10 QNAME criteria and remains separate from primary fixed-denominator retention.

All16 selected exception coordinates are in the fixed cohort and are retained regardless of new coverage. The three MAPQ60-only flags remain separately labelled from the13 original DNA-dominant exceptions.

New counts use MAPQ>=30, BQ>=25, proper-pair flag and exclusion0xF0C, direct M/=/X CIGAR coordinates, and one unambiguous ACGT bit per QNAME. Conflicting qualified bases are counted separately and excluded from ACGT depth. The clean sensitivity matches no-S CIGAR plus at least5 query bases from each aligned query edge.

compare_names checks original16 ACGT counts against frozen values and checks new frozen-name allele masks against primary count output. Original supporters receive one mutually exclusive prioritized transition; failure/absence/unmapped/reference-span-without-base categories are retained.
new_all_names_same_base is a fresh full-cohort-overlap count distinct from tracking the fixed original supporter set; these must not be conflated in prose.
Explicit source limitations state that a changed full pipeline is not necessarily a correction and that emitted records are not all hypothetical placements.

substantive_issue.impact: Auxiliary physical-query-position transition coordinates may be incorrect if equal stored query lengths conceal different terminal hard clips. Does not alter primary site allele counts or QNAME transition categories.
substantive_issue.example: Forward100-base read:10H90M and90M10H each store90bases. Stored index20 represents full-read offset30 versus20. Length equality alone cannot identify the same physical base.
substantive_issue.recommended_fix: Before reporting a physical coordinate, gate any H in either original/new alignment or reconstruct full-read hardclip offsets and verify orientation-normalized query correspondence. If omitted, label those traces indeterminate rather than reporting an exact coordinate.

resolution.description: Both original and new records must lack H CIGAR operators, have equal stored length, and have identical SHA256 of get_forward_sequence() before physical-position tracing. All other cases are explicitly not traced. Diff only adds observation metadata, trace gate and limitations; primary allele-call and QNAME outcome logic is unchanged.

editorial_requirements: Use QNAME units/read names, not independent molecules. Shared paired-end reads and PCR duplicates are not made molecularly independent by QNAME collapse.

PABPC1_linkage in compare_names is shared QNAME-set support. It does not itself establish that both alleles occupy the same qualifying alignment; the earlier original-library same-alignment check is a separate result.

For MAPQ60-only sites, the tracked allele is a sensitivity-selected allele. It is not generally unexpected under the fixed baseline DNA mixed/residual category. The script uses expected=None there, appropriately avoiding a new baseline DNA-expected label.
Do not call a strong-screen flag resolved merely because new depth falls below50, or retention corrected because a name becomes filtered, unmapped, clipped or differently placed.

Same numeric MAPQ/flag filters do not make upstream pipelines identical. References, STAR version, splice/mapping parameters and duplicate marking can differ; mapping confidence semantics (including STAR255) are not calibrated equivalence.
Ordinary records are captured only when an M/=/X block overlaps a fixed SNP; D/N-only and complete nonACGT inventories are unavailable outside the frozen-name set.
No new clinical performance, specimen identity, contamination-fraction or diagnosis inference follows from this method comparison.
nonblocking_robustness_suggestions: Assert the known2873 dominant count and4015 unique keys at runtime before emitting baseline_denominators_preserved=True; frozen metadata was independently checked here.
Assert each supporter outcome sum equals its original supporter denominator.
Empty table lists would cause compare_names.table to index rs[0]; a header-only/empty-safe writer would be more robust if physical traces are later comprehensively gated.

verified_claims: All 23,209,264 RNA read pairs were processed; 4,015 original sites remain; 3,932 meet new depth20; 83 are below20 and none has zero ACGT evidence.

The original 2,873 DNA-dominant denominator remains: old2,860/new2,805 meet depth20+90%; old2,760/new2,721 meet depth20+98%. All59 new coverage failures came from originally passing sites. There are13 original versus9 new callable sites below90%.
Of13 original exceptions,5 reach90% and8 remain below it. One new MLLT3 site, chr9:20414378, changes A24/G2 to A24/G3 at depth27, below the strong-screen depth floor.
All six stronger-site DNA, original RNA and new RNA values match the frozen and new tables. Five remain strong-screen flags; APOD does not.
PABPC1 has61/470 G and73/430 C query-name counts,61 shared new names and56 original shared names retaining both. Prose identifies shared names, not independent molecules or validated tumor mutations.
All13 original exceptions plus3 separate MAPQ60-only sites remain. The latter RNA values use matched baseline filters and are not promoted to new primary flags.
All3,426 frozen names were recovered in9,061 new named records. APOD26/27 expected-G outcomes plus1 filtered outcome, and the EXOC3/MSH3-DHFR transitions, match the produced summary.

No new placement is called a correction. APOD is described as alignment/pipeline-dependent. No identity probability, contamination fraction, clinical performance, new treatment target or diagnostic conclusion is claimed.
Resource figures match run.json in decimal MB/GB:26.8 minutes,64.1 MB selective BAM,8.40 GB peak main-pipeline RSS and4.99 GB minimum free disk.
